title: A game of cards that could change the world - All Will Rise appeals because it's unafraid to have a perspective
description: I'm a big fan of the moment when, years into a gaming subgenre's existence, people start rethinking what those games are capable of. All the expected ideas, they've been done, so the latecomers are by necessity inventors if they want to stand out. All Will Rise is one of them. In essence, it's a deck-building card game that was volcanoed into existence by the popularity of Slay the Spire several years ago, or perhaps Magic: The Gathering before, or perhaps Pokémon. title: All Meditation Spots In GTA 6
description: Sometimes, you just want to step away and relax from all the hustle and bustle in Grand Theft Auto 6. By “hustle,” we mean ransacking the vaults of banks, and by “bustle,” we mean running over hundreds of people with trucks. So, why not head to the wilderness in search of Meditation Spots? You might even find inner peace while you’re at it. In This Article How Meditation Spots work in Grand Theft Auto 6 Meditation Spots in Mariana County Meditation Spot #1: Intro to Meditation Meditation Spot #2: Smooth Sand Meditation Meditation Spots in Kelly County Meditation Spot #3: Swamp Meditation Meditation Spot #4: Worn Stone Meditation Meditation Spot #5: Red Rocks Meditation Meditation Spot in Leonard County Meditation Spot #6: Seaside Meditation Meditation Spots in Lummox County Meditation Spot #7: Waterfalls Meditation Meditation Spot #8: Jutting Cliff Meditation Meditation Spot #9: Water Wheel Meditation Meditation Spot #10: Mountain Ascent Meditation How Meditation Spots work in Grand Theft Auto 6 Meditation Spots are a type of activity that you can do when you’re not tackling missions. You simply need to go to specific areas, sit down, and then press the corresponding button prompts to complete breathing exercises. As an aside, even if Jason and Lucia are together during a run, they have to do their meditation exercises separately. Try to be patient since each process can take a while. Meditation Spots in Mariana County There are a couple of GTA 6 Meditation Spots in Mariana County. They’re on opposite ends of the zone and one of them is technically missable. Meditation Spot #1: Intro to Meditation This Meditation Spot is actually the porch/deck of Jason’s house in Key Lento. To unlock it, play through chapter 1 normally until Lucia notices that Jason seems stressed out. She’ll eventually encourage him to meditate on the porch, so follow her to start the tutorial. Take note that this sequence is missable if you leave the house instead of listening to Lucia’s prompt.…

title: How To Play Tennis And All Court Locations In GTA 6
description: Tennis was one of the most beloved minigames from Grand Theft Auto 5, and by all indications, it appeared that Rockstar Games was bringing it back for GTA 6. However, players are dozens of hours into the game by this point, and the tennis minigame has still eluded everyone. While there are plenty of golf courses and racing challenges for players to participate in, no tennis icon appears in GTA 6. However, there are several fully fleshed-out tennis courts spread across Leonida, so what exactly is going on with the tennis minigame? In This Article Can you play tennis in GTA 6? All tennis court locations in GTA 6 Courtland Park Stadium Port Vice City Ocean Beach Washington Beach Rialto Islands (Catalan Island) Can you play tennis in GTA 6? Technically, tennis is a playable minigame in GTA 6. However, it's not nearly as complete as the other minigames, such as golf, billiards, and racing. Instead, tennis looks to be in a similar spot to the basketball minigame. You can freely pick up rackets and tennis balls in GTA 6, but no location offers you the ability to play against NPCs or other characters in full-on matches. You're only able to hit the ball with the racket, and this doesn't even have to be on a tennis court. Compared to GTA 5, which lets you play hour-long matches against Michael's wife or other characters, this is quite the step down when it comes to tennis. However, Rockstar Games has said certain minigames simply couldn't be implemented in time, and it looks like they prioritized other content over tennis in GTA 6. Still, with minigames like tennis and basketball included in GTA 6, future updates or even DLC could expand on them. After all, there are plenty of tennis courts to make use of in Leonida. All tennis court locations in GTA 6 There are several tennis courts you can find and enter in GTA 6. It's at these courts where you'll be able to find a tennis racket and ball to pick up and practice your serves with. However, no matter how long you stand…

description: In the grim darkness of the week before the release of Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, developers King Art and publishers Deep Silver have released a demo model painter. It's your chance to pre-emptively run a brush over units from the new strategy game's four major factions – Orks, Adeptus Mechanicus, Necrons and Space Marines. The Imperial Guard are in the game too, but mostly as a tutorial army. What a slap in the face for the Imperium's vanilla humans. Deep Silver are calling it "the most powerful Painter in Dawn of War history", which doesn't seem all that dashing a boast given that Dawn of War 3 came out almost 10 years ago and today's PCs have a fair bit more RAM in them. You can opt for Basic Painter mode in order to quickly knock together livery for entire armies, or fire up the Advanced Painter and get stuck into the weeds of individual armour and body parts, with a choice of materials, patterns, decals and weathering. title: Hollow Knight: Silksong’s First Major Expansion Arrives December 11, And It’s Free
description: Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry has shown a first look at the upcoming Sea of Sorrow expansion. The first major--and free--expansion for Silksong takes players to a new aquatic region, with new areas to explore and new tools to master. You won't have to wait too long to play it either, as it's out on December 11. Team Cherry describes the expansion as a grand tale of high-seas adventure, full of new characters, items, and bosses. And in case that trailer isn't enough, here's a gallery of in-game screenshots for Sea of Sorrow: The Cherry Time livestream also showed off a trio of new games on the way, and they all look delightful. First up was Blokkan: Secret of the Walking City, a video game based on a comic book about a robot detective who investigates cases. It features hand-drawn art, and it plays like a love letter to the golden age of adventure games. Next up was Radio Rain, a 2D pixel-art side-scroller where you play as a young girl named Cass, trapped in a ruined, rainy world. Inspired by '80s music, Cass searches rain-spattered streets, fights mischievous creatures, and works alongside her spirit companion to find a way home. Finally, The Botanist and the Translator closed out the new reveals. As the plant detective Hatti, players will investigate a planet-spanning plant mystery alongside her trusty translator, Oliver, in this breezy, beautiful adventure.

title: Alan Wake Dev’s Forgotten TV-Action Game Hybrid Is At A Huge Discount Right Now
description: I loved Quantum Break. In fact, I dare say that I still love it to this day. Combining Remedy’s pizzazz for third-person shooters with the boldness to add TV show elements to the narrative experience, Quantum Break’s time-bending power fantasy is one that hooked me from start to finish. After playing it at launch, I let the dust settle before playing it once again in the early 2020s, and now, it’s time for another playthrough—and you may as well join me when it’s this cheap. After Alan Wake’s horror-led approach, with Stephen King vibes oozing from the entire experience, I don’t think any of us expected it to become a larger part of a connected universe. Quantum Break may not officially be part of the same universe, but it feels like the foundation of what would eventually become Remedy’s connected universe. You play as Jack Joyce, who, after catching up with his time-machine-making friend Paul Serene, is interrupted by Jack’s brother, Will, who says using it will cause time to end. Of course, if that happened, the game wouldn’t continue. Instead, both Jack and Paul are afflicted by chronon radiation, giving the pair time-related abilities. Soldiers appear, causing a ruckus on the university campus, led by an older, more dangerous Paul. Gasp! It’s no surprise that a narrative focusing on time-travel shenanigans offers, well, time-travel shenanigans. But between missions, you’ll get to see real actors playing the characters in a series-style format, which gives you a nice break between some incredibly fun missions. That’s right, Remedy’s continued prowess in third-person shooter action is still here, and the time abilities give you some truly fun ways to deal with enemies. You can send out bubbles that freeze enemies in place, fire a barrage of bullets into them, and watch them die a horrible death by countless simultaneous bullets. A dash lets you close the gap between Jack and any enemies giving you trouble from a distance, while a blast lets you levitate…

title: I Was Wrong About GTA 6
description: Some months ago, I wrote about how, even prior to its full reveal, we already knew what GTA 6 was going to be. Although not unique to the franchise by any means, GTA games had always followed a very clear formula, rarely upending it in any meaningful way. I strongly suspected that the 13-year wait for GTA 6 would result in a very pretty version of a very familiar game. As release approached, I worried that for all of the praise heaped upon its story and incredible level of detail, all of that was merely a veneer on the same game we've been playing for 25 years. And in many ways, that is true; at its most basic level, GTA 6 is still a game about driving from point A to point B, and maybe shooting some ne'er-do-wells when you get there. But I dramatically underestimated the impact of that veneer, and just how differently a familiar formula can feel when accompanied by impactful systems and relationships. The freeform nature of GTA 6's world, and the objectives you have over the course of a given mission, are largely identical to previous games. You can just drive around and make your own fun, or deal with violent drug smugglers, or pilot a boat or plane or car through a series of checkpoints. It's all very familiar on paper. But never before in a GTA game have I considered whether I have time to go and do one of those things because I have someone I care about waiting at home. Only rarely in a GTA have I decided to drive carefully, lest I face the consequences of doing almost anything I'd traditionally associate with a GTA game. So much of GTA 6's focus is on the relationship between Lucia and Jason. I quickly found myself caring about them both, and for all of Rockstar's talk of their romantic relationship being optional, I truly can't fathom playing this in a way that doesn't fully embrace their love. And the way that permeates things even in Chapter 1--the phone calls, the text messages, the interactions at home--has forced some degree of role-playing on me. I…
